summary: Ghulam Yazdani was an indologist and archaeologist. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (B.A. 1905) under J. Godfrey F. Day, C. F. Andrews, M. Ishaq, and N. A. Dehlvi. He directed the Archaeological Department of Hyderabad State (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1977–1981) and Sapienza University of Rome (1982–1985) under Raniero Gnoli, later teaching at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2000–2007).
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. After graduating from Kyoto University in 1914, he served there as lecturer (1929) and assistant professor (1935–1948), and later as professor at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya and later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He earned degrees at Kyoto University (-1935, 1953) under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki, and was a professor there (1968–1972) and at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a PhD from Stanford University (~1991–1998), where he studied under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, among others. He served as a teacher at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997).

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Madeleine Biardeau. His posts include senior fellow at the CNRS and director of the Indo-French exchange program at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme (both attested 2004).
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin (attested 2008).

Giovanni Gentile was a philosopher educated at the Scuola Normale Superiore and University of Pisa. He was a professor at Palermo (1906–1914), Pisa (1914–1917), and Sapienza (1917–1944), and served as president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (1933).

Giovanni Vacca was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the universities of Genoa and Florence, taught at Florence (1910), and held chairs in East Asian language, literature, history, and geography at Sapienza University of Rome (1911–1948).

Giovanni Verardi is an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and indologist who studied at Allahabad, BHU, and Gorakhpur universities. He taught at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (1972–1987), the University of Bologna (1981–1987), and was professor at Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

Girindrasekhar Bose studied at Presidency College, Medical College and Hospital, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta. He served as Professor of Experimental Psychology at the University of Calcutta (1917–1949) and was president of the Indian Psychoanalytic Society (1922–1953).

Gisela Emma Full is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. She studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster and served as a research fellow at the University of Frankfurt (Oder) and the Samueli Institute (attested 2013).

Gisho Nakano was an indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Junjiro Takakusu and at Kyushu University, he held professorships at Peking University (1933) and Koyasan University, where he served as president (1951, 1964).
Giti Dutt works in history and archaeology and is a PhD student at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron (attested 2026).
Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University in 2010.

Giuseppe Bardelli was an indologist and linguist who studied under Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He served as a lecturer of Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1845–1853).

Giuseppe Gasparo Mezzofanti was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna (~1789–1797). He served as a professor of languages at the University of Bologna (~1797–1831) and as Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library (1833).

Giuseppe Tucci was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Sapienza under Carlo Formichi and Giovanni Vacca, later serving as professor at Sapienza (1932) and president of the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (1947–1978).
